answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost.
